children: US crude oil inventories fell by 2.09 million barrels in the week ending October 2, after rising 1.019 million barrels in the previous week.
Commercial crude inventories excluding the SPR have declined by more than 38 million barrels over the past 25 weeks, while total US crude inventories are up nearly 13 million barrels year to date.
Another 800,000 barrels were released from the SPR, bringing total holdings to 283 million barrels.
The generally accepted operational minimum for the SPR is between 250 million and 300 million barrels.
Gasoline inventories fell by 1.37 million barrels after rising 2.991 million barrels the previous week, while distillate inventories increased by 461,000 barrels following a 286,000-barrel decline.
US oil production rose to 13.955 million bpd in the week ending September 25, from 13.939 million bpd a week earlier.

title: US Crude Inventories Fall 2.09 Million Barrels
